title: Ink: Efficient Incremental k-Critical Path Generation
problem: Critical path generation (CPG) algorithms used in static timing analysis cannot efficiently update results when circuits are incrementally modified. Existing state-of-the-art approaches require full recomputation of k critical paths from scratch rather than leveraging previous results.
motivation: Incremental CPG is essential for iterative circuit design and verification workflows where designs are continuously modified.
method: When a circuit is modified, Ink avoids recomputing all the critical paths (the longest signal routes that determine maximum circuit speed) from scratch. Instead, it examines paths from the previous calculation and identifies which ones remain similar or still valid. By reusing these existing paths, Ink skips searching most of the possible path combinations. It maintains previous results across changes, so only the affected parts need new calculations.
key_novelty: The core innovation is recognizing that critical path traces (the sequences of signal delays through circuits) stay similar between consecutive modifications, allowing previously found paths to be reused instead of recalculated.
contributions: First incremental CPG algorithm that efficiently handles circuit modifications
Path reuse and search space pruning strategies exploiting similarity across queries
22.4X speedup and 31% memory reduction compared to state-of-the-art timers
Demonstration of effectiveness on large circuit benchmarks
